analysis: The supplied units are head-side excerpts of CHANGELOG.md (lines 1619-2175), which is part of a large documentation-only change (the patch adds a v0.10.9 candidate section and history). No executable code, configuration, workflow, or threat-model files are visible in these units, so no regression can be demonstrated from them. I read the entries for security-relevant claims and found nothing that contradicts the threat model. Cluster worker protocol 2 uses packed token IDs, with both Macs required to run the same release. The changelog also records the SSD prefix cache entries: the 30-minute sliding TTL, per-checkpoint file namespaces bound to the binary and metallib hashes, restore mtime refresh and eviction changes, and the write-budget ledger. These relate to T-041 (SSD cache) and describe no change to HMAC naming, AES-GCM, KEK scope or TTL beyond 30 minutes. The sandbox and add-on entries (TB-012, TB-013) and the dev-branch signed release lane entries are consistent with the existing mitigations (Developer ID signing, notarization, source gate). The coordinator reconnect, hold and re-registration entries are availability behaviors that keep registration, attestation and cancellation unchanged. The actual code changes behind these descriptions are not in the supplied units. The changelog is only a claim about behavior and does not establish that the code matches it. Integration should check the corresponding source diffs (cluster protocol, SSD cache restore, release workflows) against T-041, TB-012, TB-013 and T-061. Coverage here is limited to documentation text and the truncated patch excerpt.
